summary_en: eole Inc. will make WOODMAN Corp. a wholly-owned subsidiary through a stock-for-stock exchange. WOODMAN reported sales of 12.8 billion yen and operating profit of 350 million yen for the nine months ended September 2026. The transaction is intended to strengthen AI data center development and immersion cooling technology capabilities. Shareholder approval is required at extraordinary general meetings of both companies scheduled for November 2026.
title_en: Notice Regarding Conclusion of Stock Exchange Agreement for Complete Subsidiary Status of WOODMAN Corp. through Stock Exchange and Changes in Major Shareholders and Lead Major Shareholder
translation_en_brief:
eole Inc. concluded a stock exchange agreement on October 15, 2026, to acquire WOODMAN Corp. as a wholly-owned subsidiary through a stock-for-stock transaction rather than a cash acquisition. eole will be the complete parent company and WOODMAN will be the complete subsidiary following regulatory approvals.

The two companies have been collaborating since January 2026 on modular AI data center projects and immersion cooling solutions. WOODMAN, established in October 2017, currently generates sales of approximately 12.8 billion yen and operating profit of 350 million yen for the fiscal year ending September 2026. The company has developed immersion cooling technologies (IMMERSIA and IMMERSIA EDGE) and possesses expertise in AI data center design, construction, and consulting. eole selected the stock exchange method to align long-term interests between both sets of shareholders and preserve cash for growth investments in AI data center development, rather than depleting capital through a cash purchase.

Following the integration, eole plans to deploy both large-scale (100MW-class) and mid-sized (2MW-class) AI data centers across Japan, leveraging WOODMAN's established land, utility networks, technical expertise, and client relationships alongside eole's GPU procurement and computing power capabilities. The transaction is subject to approval by extraordinary general meetings of both companies scheduled for November 2026, with WOODMAN's existing management team continuing operations post-acquisition.
